title: diagnostic-checkpoint-and-safe-retry-operator
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Adds a diagnostic checkpoint artifact and a safe-retry operator for automated remediation actions. Backoff, approval gating and telemetry comparisons included.
description:
Summary: This PR introduces two coordinated features to the incident-bot toolkit: (1) a lightweight diagnostic checkpoint exporter that snapshots curated telemetry + traces at defined incident points and uploads artifacts to the configured artifact store (S3/GCS); and (2) a SafeRetry operator used by automated remediation routines that enforces exponential backoff, rate limits, idempotency checks, and an optional human-approval gate before applying potentially disruptive actions.

Motivation: We frequently need reproducible, pre-mitigation snapshots to validate whether an automated remediation reduced error rates or regressed latency. Previous runs lacked standardized checkpoints and we had multiple unsafe retry implementations that caused flapping in production during incidents.

Goals: make checkpoints cheap and language-agnostic, make retries safe by default, and provide a simple A/B telemetry comparator so responders can see pre/post deltas.

Design:
- Checkpoint exporter: instrumented hook (incident_bot.checkpoint.capture) captures a short set of curated probes (top-5 traces, error-rate histogram, recent logs tail, sampled spans) and bundles into a timestamped tar.gz with metadata.json. Configurable TTL and retention; supports HMAC-signed URLs for ephemeral sharing in Slack.
- SafeRetry operator: a library component used by runbooks and automation workflows. Exposes retry(action, idempotency_token, max_attempts, backoff_policy, approval_policy). Backoff supports jittered exponential and token-bucket rate limiting. Approval_policy can require an LDAP group or a Slack interactive approval. The operator records each attempt to the checkpoint store to link attempts with telemetry.
- Pre/Post comparator: lightweight comparator that computes deltas for user-configurable signal sets (error-rate, p95 latency, queue depth) and renders a compact verdict (improved/unchanged/regressed) with confidence estimation based on sampling.

Testing & CI: Unit tests added for exporter serialization and SafeRetry state machine; integration test spins up a local fake-artifact-store and a mock Slack approver; e2e scenario included in the incident-bot test harness to exercise full flow.

Backwards compatibility: existing runbooks can opt-in by swapping their retry calls to SafeRetry; default behavior is non-blocking and mirrors prior semantics unless approval is required.

Rollout plan: staged feature flag rollout over 2 weeks; enable checkpoint upload to dev artifact store, then canary, then global. If regression detected, feature flag off and immediate rollback instructions included.

Review conversation:
- Diego: "Can we ensure checkpoint payloads are size-limited by default?" Author: "Yes — default bundle max 4MB; config overrides allowed. Added truncation for logs and span sampling to keep size bounded."
- Evelyn: "Approval flow looks good; can we add an audit entry for each manual approval?" Author: "Added audit log entry and included requestor and decision metadata in the artifact metadata.json."
- Jordan: "Can retries cause duplicate side-effects against idempotency-unaware APIs?" Author: "SafeRetry requires an idempotency_token for non-idempotent actions; without token, it refuses retry unless explicit approval policy bypass is set."
- Evelyn (after CI run): "Tests flaked in the Slack mock, re-run CI."

CI and validation:
- initial CI: flaky in integration (mock Slack timeout)
- fixed by increasing mock timeout and retrying
- final CI: all checks passed (unit, lint, integration, e2e harness)

Security review notes: Tokenized uploads use short-lived signed URLs and artifacts default to private. Approval adapters require an allowlist of approver groups.

Performance: Checkpoint capture is bounded and runs async with a 200ms sampling budget on hot paths; config allows synchronous capture for debug builds.

Post-merge actions:
- Feature flag 'diag_checkpoint' added to deploy/feature_flags/flags.yaml
- Runbook template example added to docs
- Added a small rake task to prune old artifacts per TTL

Known limitations and follow-ups:
- Current comparator is sampling-based and may miss transient improvements; plan to iterate with more robust statistical tests (ENG-3501)
- GCP KMS integration for artifact encryption planned (follow-up ticket ENG-3550)

Merge outcome: merged via squash, commit message prefixed with "feat(incident-bot): diagnostic checkpoint + safe retry".
